  ```
    {attribute: "power_supply_voltage", axis: "power_supply", values: [{condition: "mains adapter", value: {min: 220... no, 230}, unit_symbol: "V"}, ...]}
  ```

  - power_supply_voltage: 230 V AC (mains)

  - adapter_output_voltage: 9 V DC
  - battery: "6 × 1.5 V"

  - power_supply_voltage: value 230, unit V, plus config? Hmm.

  ```
    {"attribute": "power_supply_voltage", "axis": "power supply option", "values": [
      {"condition": "AC adapter (mains)", "value": {"min": 220, ...}}
    ]}
  ]
  ```

  ```
  "config_level": [
    {

      "axis": "power_supply_option",
      "values": [
        {"condition": "Mains adapter: 230 V AC 50/60 Hz input, 9 V DC output", "value": "230 V AC / 9 V DC"},

    }
  ]
  ```
  Hmm but rule 2 requires structured values. For string values that's fine ("value": "230 V AC"). But cleaner: separate attributes.

  Alternative approach: type_level:
  - mains_voltage: 230 V
  - mains_frequency: {50, 60} Hz
  - adapter_output_voltage: 9 V DC
  - battery_configuration: "6 × 1.5 V"

  ```
    }
  ```

  Then type_level: power_supply_frequency {min 50, max 60} Hz; power_supply_type "AC/DC"? The adapter output 9 V DC — put adapter_output_voltage: 9 V DC as type_level.
